metric.semantic_locality.basis: all-fragments (single-language shard; this worker computes only the Go raw counts and a self-consistent Go-side normalized figure — score_requires_comparability_gate in primary.json means the runner must still merge this with the other nine languages' shards before any common-basis figure or cross-language ranking is valid; this file does not itself satisfy that gate)
caveats: This shard covers only Go. The frozen methodology requires metrics A-D to be computed primarily on a common basis across all ten languages (interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule) and requires score_requires_comparability_gate before the score is authoritative; the runner must merge this Go figure with the other nine language shards and recompute the common-basis figure before any cross-language ranking is valid.

Lookup counts reflect the plainest idiomatic Go form selected under R10 (fewest tokens under the frozen tokenizer, ties broken by stdlib documentation order); alternative forms were not separately re-tokenized here because this worker's assigned requirement is semantic_locality only, not semantic_density (metric A), which is scored by a separate worker.

Support-level (FULL/PARTIAL/NONE) determinations referenced above (e.g. F02.P2, F12.P1, F12.P2, F14.P1, F17.P2 as PARTIAL/P-a substitutions) are asserted for internal consistency of this locality analysis but are not this worker's authoritative Capability Coverage record; the coverage worker's rubric application governs the official support level.
metric.semantic_locality.methodology_rule_applied: Per semantic_compression.md 6.1.3.C: 'Record the number of required external semantic lookups or declaration-graph hops ... required to determine the semantic facts of each probe. Lower lookup cost is better. A lookup that is optional for extra detail must not be counted; count only context required to resolve a fact in the fixed inventory.' Counted lookup kinds observed for Go in this probe set: (a) callee signature (F05.P1, explicitly frozen as a non-local lookup by the probe text itself), (b) imported stdlib definitions needed to resolve a frozen fact (e.g. math.MaxInt32's exact value/width, strconv.Atoi's failure signature, sort/slices ordering facility, os/io file-handle failure and cleanup signatures, sync/atomic's documented atomicity guarantee, cgo import "C" foreign declarations), (c) a separate-package interface/method signature lookup for the multi-unit extensibility probe F14.P3 and the visibility-boundary probe F18.P2.
metric.semantic_locality.n_L_note: All 44 probes have at least a FULL or PARTIAL Go fragment (Go lacks a few frozen capabilities, e.g. closed sum types F14.P1, deterministic destructors F17.P2, generic Optional F12.P1/F12.P2 — these are recorded as PARTIAL substitutions per R9/P-a, not NONE, so they remain in the all-fragments basis with n_L=44). No probe is scored NONE for Go in this shard's judgement; Capability Coverage support levels are the authoritative record maintained by the coverage worker, not this locality worker.
metric.semantic_locality.normalization_formula: For each probe i with raw non-local-lookup count L_i (Go), per-probe locality score_i = 100 / (1 + L_i). Probe-level scores are then averaged unweighted over the 44-probe all-fragments basis to produce the reported figure. Lower L_i -> higher score_i (100 when L_i=0). This is a fixed, language-neutral formula; the same formula and lookup-kind taxonomy is intended to be applied identically to every language's shard so the runner can merge without redefining the rule.

F01.P1.rationale: const n = 7; return n — fully local, untyped constant, no import or external declaration needed.

F01.P2.rationale: package-level var counter int64 = 0; const LIMIT int64 = 100 — both local syntax, no lookup.

F02.P1.rationale: var v int32; branch assigns 5/9; read v — all local (Go zero-initializes but the two-arm assignment before any read makes the local form self-explanatory).

F02.P2.rationale: Go has no genuinely-uninitialized safe buffer; substitute default-zeroed [16]byte, still fully local (PARTIAL under P-a, not a locality cost).

F03.P2.rationale: xs[1] = 42 — local single statement; xs's own declaration is given context per R5 and not counted.

F04.P1.rationale: port := &slot; *port = 9; return slot — local pointer aliasing, no lookup.

F04.P2.rationale: window := xs[0:3] shares the backing array — local slicing syntax.

F04.P3.rationale: allocate *T, round-trip through a one-element []* T to obtain second, compare with == — all local, builtin pointer identity.

F05.P1.rationale: Bare call f(x): per the probe's own binding scoring note, f's declaration/signature is explicitly excluded from the fragment and must be counted as a non-local (callee-signature) lookup for metric C.

F05.P2.rationale: put(cell *int32){*cell = 12}; call put(&cell) — the explicit pointer form's own full declaration is inside the measured fragment for this probe, so nothing external is needed.

F05.P3.rationale: neg declared locally as a closure capturing k; applied via an ordinary for-range loop referring to neg by name — fully local.

F06.P1.rationale: mid's full declaration is inside the fragment; int element is a value type so independence is locally evident.

F06.P2.rationale: divmod2 returns (int32,int32) — Go's native multi-return is fully local, full function body inside fragment.

F07.P2.rationale: q := a/b; m := a%b; d := float64(a)/float64(b) — local, plain conversion.

F08.P1.rationale: m := math.MaxInt32 requires import "math"; resolving the exact value/width of the named maximum is an imported-definition lookup even though the wrap-on-overflow behavior of '+' itself is general Go-spec knowledge rather than a per-construct lookup.

F08.P2.rationale: explicit local guard: if b == 0 { q = 0 } else { q = a / b } — fully local, no stdlib checked-division form exists in Go so rung (ii) is used.

F09.P1.rationale: eq := s1 == s2 — Go's built-in string == is content comparison; no import needed to know this (guaranteed by the language spec directly, not a per-site lookup).

F09.P2.rationale: Descending sort requires import "sort" (or "slices") and an explicit comparator/reverse descriptor; resolving whether the operation mutates in place or allocates requires consulting that package's documentation — one imported-definition lookup.

F10.P1.rationale: small := int32(big) — plain narrowing conversion, local; Go has no stdlib checked int64->int32 conversion, so rung (ii) applies with no import.

F10.P2.rationale: sum := float64(i) + d — local explicit conversion, no import.

F11.P1.rationale: e := xs[i] — built-in indexing, panics on out-of-range per language spec, no import.

F11.P2.rationale: part := xs[1:4] — built-in slicing, shares the backing array; local.

F12.P1.rationale: Go has no generic Optional in the standard library; substitute a *int32 with nil for absence and a local nil-check for the fallback — fully local (PARTIAL under P-a).

F12.P2.rationale: h declared locally; applied via an explicit local nil-check substitute (no stdlib optional-map operation exists) — fully local (PARTIAL under P-a).

F13.P1.rationale: strconv.Atoi is called and its error propagated; resolving that it can fail and how requires consulting strconv's documented signature — one imported-definition lookup.

F13.P2.rationale: Same strconv.Atoi call, handled locally with if err != nil; still requires the same imported-definition lookup to know the failure shape.

F14.P1.rationale: Go has no closed sum types; substitute an open Shape interface with Circle/Rect structs, all declared locally within the fragment (PARTIAL under P-a) — no external lookup.

F14.P2.rationale: type switch on the interface value, no default arm — fully local; Go does not statically check switch exhaustiveness (locality is unaffected, that gap is charged elsewhere).

F14.P3.rationale: Tri is implemented in a separate package against the shapes package's Area-returning interface; satisfying that interface requires consulting the interface's method signature declared in the other unit — one imported-definition lookup.

F15.P1.rationale: func head[T any](xs []T) T { return xs[0] } used at int32 and string — Go 1.18+ generics are fully local, no import.

F15.P2.rationale: max_of[T cmp.Ordered](a, b T) T requires import "cmp" (or golang.org/x/exp/constraints) to resolve what the Ordered constraint actually requires — one imported-definition lookup.

F15.P3.rationale: Named interface and A, B implementations declared locally within the fragment; []Named{A{}, B{}} and dispatch are all local.

F16.P1.rationale: xs := []int32{1,2,3}; manual for-range summation loop — Go's standard library has no generic Sum, so the local loop form is used; no import.

F16.P2.rationale: map[string]int32 literal, range iteration, v, ok := mp["b"] comma-ok lookup — all built-in map syntax, no import.

F17.P1.rationale: os.Open + defer f.Close() + io.ReadAll(f) — resolving the possible-failure and lifetime guarantees of these calls requires consulting the os/io package documentation, an imported-definition lookup (counted once for the pair).

F17.P2.rationale: Go has no deterministic destructor; substitute a Handle struct with a Close method invoked via defer inside the block, incrementing released — fully local (PARTIAL under P-a).

F18.P1.rationale: import "fmt"; fmt.Println("x") — although the import line is inside the measured fragment, resolving what fmt.Println actually does (which side effects, which failure behavior) requires consulting fmt's own documentation — one imported-definition lookup.

F18.P2.rationale: util.PubAdd(2,3) called from a separate package main; util's exported/unexported boundary and PubAdd's signature must be looked up in the util package — one imported-definition lookup, using the frozen multi-unit recipe.

F19.P1.rationale: two goroutines each sending on an unbuffered channel, joined by receiving from both channels and summing — built-in language primitives (go, chan, <-), no import required.

F19.P2.rationale: sync/atomic.AddInt64 (or sync.Mutex) is required for the documented race-free guarantee; resolving that guarantee requires consulting the sync/atomic package documentation — one imported-definition lookup.

F20.P1.rationale: cgo import "C" with a cgo comment declaring int abs(int); resolving the C ABI/foreign-boundary facts requires consulting cgo's documented behavior — one lookup.

F20.P2.rationale: //export add2 cgo directive under -buildmode=c-shared; resolving the exact exported-symbol/ABI guarantee requires consulting cgo export documentation — one lookup.
